title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navi

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, Eq. (2) and the accompanying Frustum Culling description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated removal condition is inverted for the important case of a newly observed occluder: an old feature at depth z_c behind the current observed surface d_{u,v} has z_c > d_{u,v}+delta and therefore does not satisfy the stated condition z_c < min(d_{u,v}+delta, Delta); it is retained even though it is occluded by a closer new surface. Conversely, unchanged points at the currently observed surface (z_c approximately d_{u,v}) satisfy the condition and are removed. This contradicts the claimed ability to discard stale features for object motion/occlusion. A correct visibility-based replacement procedure would normally cull all old points in the visible ray segment or, at minimum, cull points inconsistent with the newly measured depth using the opposite depth relation for occluded points.

The contrastive-loss equations have undefined and inconsistent indexing and symbols. The prose introduces a 3D instance feature E_i, but Eqs. (5)–(7) use O_i without defining it as E_i. The losses sum i=1 to I while the candidate logits are indexed j=1 to J and the cross-entropy target is i. CrossEntropy({score_j}_{j=1}^J, i) is only defined if i is a valid index in 1..J and if the positive language/teacher feature is guaranteed to occupy candidate index i; neither condition is specified. Moreover, I was previously defined as the number of image patches (I=24x24), not the number of instances. Thus the displayed objectives are not mathematically well-defined as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.6, paragraph 'Robustness to Noise' following Table 7
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says that the authors 'perform ablation by degrading the quality of 3D instance and zone embeddings through feature dropout and spatial jitter' and that 'Table 7 shows' substantially greater degradation when representation quality is compromised. Table 7 contains only four conditions defined by SLAM Noise and Depth Noise; it has no feature-dropout condition, no spatial-jitter condition, and no representation-quality results. The claimed comparison therefore is not supported by the table cited for it.

The paper states that Dynam3D improves SR over g3D-LF and Uni-NaVid by 'approximately 1-2%.' Table 1 reports R2R-CE validation SRs of 52.9 for Dynam3D, 47.2 for g3D-LF, and 47.0 for Uni-NaVid. These are improvements of 5.7 and 5.9 percentage points, respectively, not 1-2 percentage points. If relative percentages were intended, they are about 12%, not 1-2% either.

The paper claims that Dynam3D outperforms NaVid by 'approximately 3-5%' SR on REVERIE-CE and NavRAG-CE. Table 2 gives 40.1 versus 26.6 SR on REVERIE-CE, a 13.5-percentage-point improvement, and 24.7 versus 19.4 on NavRAG-CE, a 5.3-point improvement. The REVERIE claim is substantially inconsistent with the reported table.

The pre-exploration protocol explicitly collects observations at 'the navigable viewpoints annotated in the Matterport3D dataset' to construct a representation of 'the entire scene' before evaluation. This gives Dynam3D privileged test-environment coverage not available in the ordinary online-navigation setting. Yet Table 3 juxtaposes these privileged-setting results with standard no-pre-exploration NaVid results, and the surrounding discussion frames the gains as evidence of the method's advantage. A valid comparative claim requires every baseline to receive equivalent pre-exploration data and compute/memory opportunities, and requires the results to be labeled as an oracle/privileged-map setting rather than ordinary VLN performance. The text itself acknowledges insufficient controls and possible environment memorization, confirming that the reported comparison is not currently interpretable as a fair method comparison.

Reference [52] is XTuner, a training toolkit, not a LLaVA-Phi-3-mini model paper or model release. Reference [53] is the Phi-3 technical report, which documents the language model family but not the claimed LLaVA-Phi-3-mini multimodal architecture. The central VLM is therefore not correctly cited or attributable from the provided references; the paper needs the actual LLaVA-Phi model/source citation and a clear account of its visual encoder/projector.
